guide.summary: Todoist documents user-authorized OAuth2 for external apps: each customer authorizes their own account, then the app exchanges the code for a token. The least-privilege documented scope for listing active tasks is data:read, which covers tasks and supports the Get Tasks endpoint with cursor pagination. The app must be registered (App Management Console, or RFC 7591 dynamic registration for multi-tenant clients) before the authorization flow can be tested. Write, delete and team-administration actions are excluded and no scope beyond data:read is required. Setup and execution are untested.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels and filters. The write-capable data:read_write scope includes data:read, but the read-only listing action needs only data:read.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles for connected individual accounts

data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a token
steps.detail: POST the code to the documented token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and code. Include redirect_uri when the registered flow requires it. The successful response is HTTP 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, and for refresh-enabled apps expires_in and refresh_token. Store the token securely. This is an unexecuted authorization step until a real customer completes consent.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token and token_type Bearer; the token is stored only for the authorizing customer.

steps.title: Read the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with a bearer token and limit. Map the user's task title to the content property of each object in the results array. next_cursor marks more pages. This read is nonmutating. Boundary check: the same token must not be able to create or modify tasks; verify by inspecting that the granted scope is data:read and by sending no write requests.
steps.doneWhen: The response has results where each task has content, and next_cursor is either a string (more pages) or null.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange of the authorized customer

next_cursor: cursor for the next page, null at the end

steps.title: Read the next page of active tasks using next_cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same request with the same limit, adding cursor set to next_cursor from the previous response. Continue until next_cursor is null, which marks the end of results. One or two pages is not a full listing. Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor=next_cursor from each prior response, preserving limit and any other parameters. Stop when next_cursor is null.
steps.doneWhen: A page returns with next_cursor null, indicating all active task titles have been read. next_cursor is null on the final page. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
